meta.title: Spell It, Bill!
meta.textType: story: a spelling test, with word parts and a result that the text does not state

paragraphs: On Wednesday, March tenth, at seven o'clock in the morning, Pat sat at the kitchen table. He held a word card, and May sat next to him with a list. Pat had a spelling test at school that day. The green parrot Bill sat on the back of a chair and looked at the card. Bill could speak, but he could not spell. "Spell the first word," said May. "B-E-C-A-U-S-E," said Pat. Bill repeated the letters, but he said O instead of A. "No, Bill! It is A, not O," said Pat. "Shall we make a rap for it?" asked May. Pat thought for a moment, and then he began to rap. "Big elephants can always understand small elephants!" "That is the first letter of each word in because," said May. Bill repeated the rap, and he did not forget a word.

May opened her notebook to a page with the title "Spelling." She wrote two lines with a pencil. "Word parts help," she told Pat. "If you know happy, you can guess unhappy." "The beginning un means not, so unhappy means not happy." "Teach is inside teacher, and er shows a person who does it." Pat copied the two lines on a sheet of paper, and his writing was big and round. "It is important to check each letter," said May. Bill took the card with "friend" and flew to the top of the cupboard. "Bill, get back here!" said Pat. Bill dropped the card on the table and said, "Friend, friend!" Pat laughed, put the card in his bag, and ran to school.

At two o'clock, Pat's teacher gave the test papers back. In the evening, Pat came into the kitchen with his school bag on his back. He put his paper under his lunch box on the table. "It was OK," he said. May saw the corner of the paper, and she lifted it.
There was a green star on it, and under the star were the words "nine out of ten." "Nine out of ten is not just OK," said May. Pat looked at the floor, and he smiled a little.

"Which word was wrong?" asked May. "Friend," said Pat. "I forgot the I." "One wrong word is not a fail," said May. Bill looked at the green star and said, "Friend!" Pat took the paper from May and put it on the table, next to his lunch box.
text.summary: Pat practices for a spelling test at the kitchen table with May and the parrot Bill. May shows him how word parts help, and in the evening she finds the paper that he hides under his lunch box.
